name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 11 No 32

clue.text: Deaf or daft? — that’s a hat
Niche for a man at bay
Bird hopping on calf
Fat-head can follow employment without being holy nuisance in the home
King putting weight back on; so is Granny
When somewhere to write is what we need, distracted cries to anger lead
Monarch to whom uneasy lies may be attributed
Gathered from our lad’s fig tree
Branch member
Oriental joke about a little instant coffee
Master with animal is married — to the bottle
Seal with a pain put into empty chalet
Shiner put companion in need of a stiffener
Trainer turning rough about the old censor
Fruit crumble for little George and little Amold
The wave needed to achieve prosperity
Upset mineral and highball at dance
Make a show home, perhaps, allowing a French income
Goes in front of Queen to measure point on tracks
What the fowls eat amounts to very little
Anything H. T. Weaver may have produced
Note on gold in a passage from Pilgrim’s Progress
Multiformity of Biblical law?
One-time President declares himself to be lying in wait
Key cut in the twinkling of an eye
Last actor to go over the top and far away
